A savings promotion is a rate window: compare the interest dollars after it ends

Trace identical deposits through a promotional savings account and a steady-rate alternative, then test promotional length, balance caps and the ongoing rate.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore a savings promotion and the rate after it ends

Interactive planning lab

Promotion account: first twelve months’ interest$671.09
Promotion account: full-horizon interest$1,264.73
Ending balance advantage over steady account-$321.82

Two hypothetical savings accounts receive the same initial deposit and month-end contributions. Quoted rates are nominal annual percentages divided by 12; interest is credited monthly on opening balances. For the opening promotional months, the entered promotional rate applies up to the eligible-balance cap and the base rate applies above it; afterward the base rate applies to all funds. The steady account uses its own constant rate. No actual product, eligibility test, new-money rule, fees, tax, access delay or deposit-coverage determination is modeled.

The central idea

An annualized headline rate describes a rate, not a guaranteed one-year interest amount. The rate window, eligible balance and later rate determine the cash earned.

01

Put the rate and its end date on the same page

A savings advertisement can quote an annual percentage while making that rate available for only a few months. The planning comparison needs both pieces: how the rate is expressed and how long it applies to money that is actually eligible.

The FCAC’s savings-account guide discusses introductory rates and comparing account terms. A promotion should therefore be read alongside the ongoing rate and any conditions, rather than treated as an indefinitely available return.

The two accounts here are invented. They receive the same opening CAD 20,000 and the same CAD 500 at each month-end. One pays a hypothetical 5% annual quoted rate for four opening model months on up to CAD 50,000, then 2%. The comparison pays a constant 3%. These figures are selected assumptions, not current offers or a ranking of savings products.

02

Translate an annual quote into the modeled interest dollars

The model divides the quoted annual rate by twelve, credits interest on the opening monthly balance and then adds the month-end deposit. This represents nominal annual rates with monthly crediting over equal model months. It does not reproduce an account’s daily-balance calculation or its actual month lengths.

With no additional deposits, CAD 20,000 at a 5% nominal annual rate for four monthly credits earns about CAD 335.42. It does not earn CAD 1,000 simply because the quoted annual rate is 5%. That larger amount would be a simple full-year calculation before considering the actual crediting convention.

If the same balance subsequently earns 2% for eight model months, its full twelve-month interest is about CAD 608.15. The example illustrates why a promotional rate cannot be applied to the entire horizon after the promotion has expired. The interactive default also includes deposits, so its interest dollars differ from this no-deposit teaching example.

03

Separate money saved from interest credited

After twenty-four CAD 500 deposits, both default accounts have received CAD 32,000 of capital: the initial CAD 20,000 plus CAD 12,000 of later contributions. The contribution line stays identical across the two choices.

The promotion account ends at about CAD 33,264.73, including CAD 1,264.73 in interest. The steady account ends at about CAD 33,586.55, including CAD 1,586.55 in interest. The difference is about CAD 321.82 in favour of the steady account within this selected window.

A larger ending balance caused by depositing more would be a different comparison. Holding contributions equal makes this difference attributable to the modeled interest rules. The charts do not add an assumed transfer to a new promotion after the first one ends, and they do not assume the ongoing rate changes later.

04

Check which dollars receive the promotional rate

During the entered promotional months, this model applies the promotion rate to the smaller of the opening balance and the selected cap. Any excess earns the base rate. Afterward, the entire opening balance earns the base rate.

That is one explicitly chosen tier formula. Actual promotions may define new money, eligible customers, deposit dates or qualifying transactions differently. A balance in the account is not by itself evidence that the whole amount qualifies. Read the applicable offer before replacing the hypothetical cap with a real one.

Interest credited earlier becomes part of the next month’s opening balance in the calculation. It can therefore use some of the eligible cap. Setting the cap to zero removes the promotional tier entirely. If a selected promotional rate is below the base rate, the model applies that lower rate to the eligible tier rather than silently substituting a better rate.

05

Read the later interest blocks and the sensitivity matrix

The default promotion account earns about CAD 671.09 during months one through twelve, compared with CAD 691.51 in the steady account. During months thirteen through twenty-four, the figures are about CAD 593.65 and CAD 895.04. The early headline advantage does not persist through this full comparison.

The bar pairs keep each period’s interest separate. If the selected horizon leaves a final period shorter than twelve months, its exact month range is labelled and the amount is not annualized. Comparing unequal blocks as if both covered a full year would distort the result.

The matrix changes only promotional length and the base rate. Each cell reports the promotion account’s ending balance minus the same steady-account endpoint. Negative values indicate a lower ending balance, not a loss of contributed capital. A matrix cell is a conditional calculation, not the probability of obtaining a future offer.

06

Make the comparison practical before moving cash

Confirm the promotion’s start and end dates, the eligible amount and the normal rate. Include account and transfer charges when relevant. This example excludes both charges and tax, so its interest is a gross amount available before those adjustments.

Also check when transferred funds become accessible. A savings account chosen for near-term bills needs more than an attractive annual quote: the money must be usable when payment is due. The model credits every monthly deposit without a hold or transfer delay.

Keep a reminder before the promotional window ends and compare the next available choices using the same cash-flow assumptions. The central task is to reconcile the rate, time, balance and actual interest dollars. That produces a more useful comparison than choosing the largest number in an advertisement.
